svg.text: Figure C — Trust boundaries and threat model (Brier v0)
Three tiers of assurance. Only tier 1 is enforced by cryptography. Tier 2 is currently unenforced. Tier 3 is a single key.
TIER 1 — CRYPTOGRAPHICALLY GUARANTEED
Holds against a fully malicious operator. No trust required. Verified on-chain; tampering rejected (4/4 soundness checks).
Calibration-head execution
halo2/KZG proof, 2^15 rows
verifyProof = 684,696 gas
prove 2.09 s · proof 17.4 KB
Guarantees: given logit L,
head(vk) maps L → attested c
Slash arithmetic
BrierMath, WAD fixed point
no unchecked blocks; 543 gas
monotonicity + properness
Guarantees: slash is exactly
stake·(c−o)², capped, no overflow
NOT covered by tier 1
• the base classifier (not in circuit)
• provenance of the input logit L
• truthfulness of the applicant features
• the SHAP vector (hash-committed only)
A fabricated L yields a valid proof.
ThreatModel.t.sol::test_tier1_marginIsUnverified…
TIER 2 — ECONOMICALLY ASSUMED
Holds only if the operator is rational AND the assumption is actually enforced in code. One of these is not.
Assumption A — honest confidence reporting
Brier is strictly proper, so expected loss is minimised at
the operator's true belief. Verified numerically at p=0.3, 0.7.
STATUS: enforced by the payoff structure —
but only for decisions that are actually disputed, and only
if dispute selection is independent of the reported c.
Assumption B — stake is available when slashed
Requires the operator cannot exit before a dispute lands.
STATUS IN v0: BROKEN — NOT ENFORCED.
withdraw() has no unbonding period, no lock, no delay.
An operator watching the mempool can withdraw the full
stake before openDispute() is mined. Slash then hits 0.
demonstrated: ThreatModel.t.sol::test_tier2_operatorCanFrontRunDispute… (98.01 ETH → 0)
TIER 3 — FULLY TRUSTED (no cryptographic or economic guarantee whatsoever)
A single key decides who loses money. Everything in tier 1 and tier 2 is downstream of this decision.
Dispute outcome
StakePool.resolveDispute(id, upheld) — onlyAdmin
No jury. No oracle. No evidentiary standard. No appeal.
A dishonest admin can slash an honest operator to zero, or
shield a miscalibrated one indefinitely.
demonstrated: ThreatModel.t.sol::test_tier3_adminCanSlashAnHonestOperator
Ground truth for a loan rejection
The counterfactual is unobservable: a rejected applicant
never demonstrates repayment. "The decision was wrong"
has no on-chain referent.
Unsolved — not merely unimplemented.
Cheapest attack against v0 (does not require breaking any cryptography)
1. Report an honest-looking confidence and attest with a valid proof over a fabricated logit (tier 1 does not bind L).
2. Watch the mempool; on seeing openDispute(), front-run it with withdraw() — tier 2 assumption B is unenforced.
3. Failing that, rely on the admin key (tier 3) to resolve the dispute favourably. Total cryptographic work required: none.
